Captions and headlines are TEMPLATES: prose plus {{fact}} placeholders that ui/panels/more.js resolves from the committed JSON at view time, each with its honesty label; {{chip:LABEL:cite}} labels a prose claim; [[...]] is an optional clause, dropped whole until the data it names is built (never a guess). `headline` is one sentence: the P1 beat bar shows it with the full caption one click away, and on P1 beats it says what the on-screen story line says. No caption, headline or title carries a bare digit (ui/test/p2.test.js). t0/t1 are the video clock. A refuted expectation is stated as measured, never asserted.

beats.title: The problem
beats.label: REAL
beats.headline: ERCOT sends one number per zone and checks no street transformer, yet Base's Houston batteries already move {{houstonBlock}} together.
beats.caption: ERCOT dispatches one number per load zone and does not check feeders {{chip:REAL:ERCOT base points are per resource and load zone; no feeder or service-transformer check}}. Base's own Houston fleet already moves as one block: its charge reached {{houstonBlock}}. Our naive branch splits that number with no feeder check, all at once at the onset {{chip:ASSUMPTION:Base's real split is not public (build prompt 12 Q5); never implies Base charges this way today}}. Street A–D: {{streetHomes}} homes on {{streetTfs}} service transformers, every home with a battery, in a fleet of {{fleetSize}}. The scale ladder: A's battery charge at once, {{scaleLadderKW}}, as a share of each scale: {{scaleLadder}}. What overloads one service transformer does not register at the zone.

beats.title: Afternoon peak: relief at its true size
beats.label: SIM
beats.headline: {{reliefT}}: one home's spike pushes transformer A over nameplate, and its own batteries bring it back to {{reliefAware}}.
beats.caption: At {{reliefT}}, with no batteries, transformer A reaches {{reliefNone}} of nameplate: over nameplate for {{reliefMinutesNone}} (amber; not a failure). The driver is one home's load, {{reliefDriverHome}} (SMART-DS profile {{reliefDriverProfile}}), and the same profile runs at {{reliefDriverShared}}: one shape, not two pieces of evidence. Feeder-aware, at {{reliefT}} A reads {{reliefAware}}, and its own batteries discharge up to {{reliefKWPeak}}. {{unrelievedTf}} has no battery and stays over nameplate; the next-battery view answers that.

beats.title: When transformers peak vs when prices peak
beats.label: SIM
beats.headline: Transformers peak at {{insightTfHour}}, prices at {{insightPriceHour}}: a market-only plan leaves the street's peak alone.
beats.caption: Across August, transformers most often hit their monthly peak at {{insightTfHour}}; the day's highest price most often falls at {{insightPriceHour}}. {{insightVerdict}}

beats.title: Evening price peak: naive back-feed
beats.label: SIM
beats.headline: At the price peak naive sells all at once and back-feeds the street to {{naiveBackfeedMax}}; feeder-aware stays at {{awareBackfeedMax}}.
beats.caption: The market plan discharges every battery in the highest-priced intervals ({{dischargeSlots}}). Watch the batteries turn violet with an out-arrow: they are sending power out. Naive, all at once, the street's back-feed reaches {{naiveBackfeedMax}}: back-feed is an overload too. Feeder-aware caps export by headroom: the worst street reading while a transformer is actually exporting is {{awareBackfeedMax}}.

beats.title: The price collapse: naive rebound
beats.label: SIM
beats.headline: {{onsetT}}: the price drops to {{onsetPrice}}, every battery charges at once, and transformers overload: worst {{naiveMax}}.
beats.caption: The price falls from {{eveningPeakPrice}} at {{eveningPeakT}} to {{onsetPrice}} at {{onsetT}}, the charge onset. The story line walks it: price drops, every battery charges at once (bolts on every cabinet), transformers overload (meters sticking out of their boxes). The worst service transformer reaches {{naiveMax}} ({{naiveMaxTf}} at {{naiveMaxT}}): {{naiveNormalEvents}} normal-tier events and {{naiveEmergencyTfs}} transformers past the emergency rating. This rule's fuse opens above {{fusePct}} for {{fuseMinutes}}; it operated on {{naiveProtection}} transformers. Grid check: minimum service voltage {{naiveVmin}}, so {{naiveVoltVerdict}}; after the onset the feeder head peaks at {{naiveHeadOnset}}.

beats.title: The price collapse: feeder-aware rotation
beats.label: SIM
beats.headline: {{onsetT}}: the price drops, the room is checked first[[, {{onsetDeferredKW}} waits]], batteries take turns, and {{awareBatteryNormal}} overloads are caused by batteries.
beats.caption: Feeder-aware: before sending charge, check each transformer's room and send only what fits. [[At {{onsetT}} naive sends {{onsetNaiveKW}} at once; feeder-aware sends {{onsetAwareKW}} and holds back {{onsetDeferredKW}} for later in the night. ]]On street A–D the first charge reaches each transformer at {{chargeOrder}}; the controller log names every grant and hand-off. Battery-caused normal-tier events: {{awareBatteryNormal}}; emergency: {{awareBatteryEmergency}}. {{awareVerdict}} Charged by the morning deadline: {{awareCharged}}. [[Energy value tonight {{energyAware}}, against naive's {{energyNaive}}. ]]What the controller sees: {{controllerView}}.

beats.title: Pieces fail mid-balance
beats.label: SIM
beats.headline: A battery goes silent, an EV plugs in, our controller stalls: still {{faultsBatteryNormal}} battery-caused overloads.
beats.caption: At {{faultCommsT}} the battery at {{faultCommsHome}} goes silent holding a {{faultCommsKW}} command: stale after {{staleS}}, expired and idle with backup armed after {{ttlS}}, and {{faultCover}}. At {{faultHotT}} {{faultHotTf}} runs hot ({{evKW}} of new load for {{faultHotMinutes}}). {{faultHotOutcome}} At {{faultStallT}} our controller stalls for {{stallMin}}; every command expires on schedule. Battery-caused normal-tier events: {{faultsBatteryNormal}}; emergency: {{faultsBatteryEmergency}}.

beats.title: Useful capacity and dark homes
beats.label: SIM
beats.headline: Naive passes the feeder cable's rating at {{capNaiveCableAt}} batteries; feeder-aware fits {{capAware}} with {{capAwareOdssCaused}} battery-caused events in OpenDSS.
beats.caption: How many batteries fit before the grid is harmed? Naive: the feeder cable passes its rating at {{capNaiveCableAt}} batteries (per-phase estimate), and transformers break before the screening count of {{capNaiveScreen}}: OpenDSS found {{capNaiveOdssCaused}} battery-caused events and the cable at {{capNaiveOdssHead}} there. Feeder-aware fits {{capAware}}, {{capAwareStop}}; OpenDSS measured {{capAwareOdssCaused}} battery-caused events, the cable at {{capAwareOdssHead}} at most, and the lowest home voltage {{capAwareVmin}}, at the ANSI edge. Protection may operate {{chip:ASSUMPTION:fuse rule, round-1 world-sim}} in {{protectionWhere}}.

beats.title: Money, labelled
beats.label: DERIVED
beats.headline: Sell at the evening peak, buy back after the fall: tonight feeder-aware earned {{energyAware}}[[, {{awareMoreTonight}} more than naive]], with {{awareBatteryNormal}} battery-caused overloads.
beats.caption: Batteries earn by selling in the evening's priciest intervals and buying back after the price falls. Tonight's energy value: naive {{energyNaive}}, feeder-aware {{energyAware}}[[ (feeder-aware sold {{soldAware}} at the peak and bought back {{boughtAware}}; {{perBatteryAware}} a battery)]]. [[Across {{daysCount}} real ERCOT evenings, feeder-aware earned more than naive {{daysAwareMoreEvery}}, {{daysAwareSafe}}; naive overloaded a transformer on {{daysNaiveBroke}} of them. ]][[One Core cycling every evening of this year so far would have earned {{perCoreYear}}, {{top10Share}} of it on the ten best evenings: the money comes from a few price spikes. ]]A's local relief would have earned at most {{reliefOpportunity}} at the price peak. CoServ, GVEC and Austin Energy pay for system peak, coincident peaks and arbitrage, not local relief {{chip:REAL:docs/research-report.md:215-224}}: local relief is an unpriced opportunity {{chip:ASSUMPTION:no sourced price in our material}}. Pick another evening with the day chip in the where-to-charge view, or from the evenings card on this page.

beats.title: How Base plugs it in tomorrow
beats.label: SIM
beats.headline: One file beside the install queue, one function behind the zone base point, and OpenDSS checks every step in {{msPerStep}}.
beats.caption: The siting file sits beside the install queue; allocate() sits behind the zone base point, deterministic, no model in the loop. It needs {{controllerView}}. One OpenDSS solve takes {{msPerSolve}} and one full step {{msPerStep}}, measured on a shared machine; allocate() at the largest synthetic fleet takes {{allocateLargest}}.
